bullets.title: S&P 500 sells off 1%; VIX spikes to 21 on NVDA/export shock
bullets.body: The S&P 500 dropped 1% to 7,486 and VIX jumped 9.4% to 21.12 as a combination of NVDA leadership turmoil, new BIS chip export rules, and macro regime concerns hit risk assets. SOXX fell ~4% on the day, semis broadly sold off, and crypto/Bitcoin futures dropped ~7%.

bullets.title: BIS issues new interim final rule tightening AI chip export controls; closes offshore compute loophole
bullets.body: The Commerce Department issued an interim final rule requiring export licenses for advanced AI chip/server sales to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil, and restricts remote cloud access to US compute for entities tied to Country Group D:5 or Macau. The Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule was formally rescinded; new rule goes into effect in 90 days. Rule exempts US-headquartered company shipments (covering ~62% of NVDA's customer revenue) but hits SE Asian neoclouds hardest.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO succession chaos: Bessent demands external hire; Jensen discussing return; board eyes ARM's Haas
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent is pushing for an external CEO at NVIDIA, flagging 'seemingly illicit' chip sales through SE Asian data centers. Jensen Huang is reportedly discussing a return with confidants and Silicon Valley is lobbying the White House; prediction markets show Huang at 17% (vs ARM's Rene Haas at 20%). Trump told press Huang returning 'wouldn't be a bad idea.' NVDA's interim CEO Colette Kress is reportedly cutting startup and infrastructure financing, putting a ~$500M lending consortium in flux.

bullets.title: Cross-asset signals shift to 'Quad 4' regime; macro bears flag sell-the-rally setup
bullets.body: Dollar rallying to 52-week highs, commodities breaking down (copper, BCOM, oil), and curve flattening on hawkish 2yr repricing (second hike priced for January) all point to a growth+inflation-falling 'Quad 4' regime per Hedgeye/OPCO. CTA Nasdaq exposure near maximum short; hedge fund L/S net leverage at the 5th percentile; global systematic exposure fell from $350B to $212B, the lowest of the year. The tactical call is to sell rallies rather than buy dips, with SPX 7,500 as the key breakdown level.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley raises S&P 500 PT to 8,700; names Industrials top sector pick
bullets.body: MS CIO Mike Wilson lifted the 12-month S&P 500 price target to 8,700 (19x forward EPS of $458), citing healthy EPS growth (2026E $369, +34%; 2027E $420, +14%), lower oil, stabilizing rate volatility, and broadening AI adoption (44% of S&P 500 companies cited quantifiable AI benefits, up from 32%). Industrials are the top sector pick; financials and consumer discretionary also favored. MS Global Strategy concurrently raised global equities to 'Maximum Overweight.'

bullets.title: SemiAnalysis cuts 2028-2030 AI accelerator forecasts by 28-41%; ~$1.6T cumulative spend removed
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis revised down AI accelerator forecasts by 28-41% for 2028-2030, cutting cumulative 2027-2030 capex by ~$1.6 trillion, driven primarily by price deflation and financing constraints rather than demand collapse. AI spending still grows 60% in 2027 but slows to 21% in 2028 and 5% in 2029. NVIDIA bears the brunt; Broadcom and Amazon internal ASIC programs are relatively insulated. Over 80% of anticipated AI capex through 2030 will require external financing.

bullets.title: Semis priced for pessimism: 11x 2028E vs. 16x S&P 500; hedge funds near max short NDX
bullets.body: Semiconductor valuations have compressed to 11x 2028 earnings versus 16x for the S&P 500 despite 31% consensus earnings growth. NVDA now trades at the lowest valuation among large AI stocks. The semis earnings beat rate is 93.3% but beats are generating negative excess returns for a second consecutive quarter, with PE compression—not fundamentals—as the dominant return driver. Korean memory stocks flagged as particularly oversold.

bullets.title: JPMorgan forecasts US headline CPI at 3.8% YoY in Nov 2026; core PCE ticks up to 3.3%
bullets.body: JPMorgan's monthly inflation forecasts show US headline CPI moderating to 3.8% YoY in November (from 4.0% in October) on a sharp deceleration in monthly m/m SA CPI to 0.04% (from 0.35%). However, core PCE nudges up to 3.3% YoY (from 3.2%), and global ex-China/Turkey headline CPI holds at 4.0%. Eurozone and UK CPI both running at 4.0% YoY.

bullets.title: Empire Manufacturing falls 18pts to 7.8 headline but ISM-adj at healthy 55.3; capex plans improve
bullets.body: November Empire State Manufacturing headline dropped 18 points to 7.8 (new orders -20pts to 3.0, shipments -4pts to 8.8), though the ISM-equivalent measure only fell 2.5pp to 55.3. Capital expenditure plans improved to 23%, labor demand surged, and the margin proxy improved—offering a mixed but not recessionary read. MS tracks November ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.4, down from October's 55.5.

bullets.title: Anthropic (ANT) IPO roadshow: $61B valuation, $70-$78 price range, NASDAQ listing
bullets.body: Anthropic filed for IPO at a ~$61B valuation with a $70–$78 price range on 825M shares (97% primary). Ticker ANT on NASDAQ; group investor webinar scheduled November 17. Bookrunners: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Citi, Barclays, Wells Fargo. OpenAI annualized revenue run rate meanwhile grew ~70% q/q in 3Q to close to $50B, with enterprise revenue doubling q/q.

bullets.title: Goldman Sachs favors S&P 500 ex-AI enablers (SPXXAI) over traditional defensives for defensive rotation
bullets.body: GS argues traditional defensives now trade at 18x forward earnings (above 90th-percentile historically) and are expensive for downside protection. They prefer S&P ex-AI enablers (SPXXAI), which spans financials, healthcare, industrials, consumer, and energy, as a higher-quality defensive expression with earnings growth outside concentrated AI leadership.

bullets.title: Data center buildout: BXDC acquires $5B AWS portfolio; moratoriums threaten pipeline in Georgia and Texas
bullets.body: Blackstone's BXDC closed its inaugural acquisition—a 75% stake in a 647MW, 13-building AWS sale-leaseback for ~$3.75B at a 7.0% cap rate and 12-year WALT. Simultaneously, Georgia's Democratic governor-elect and Texas's incoming governor are imposing data center moratoriums, dampening what has been the largest construction pipeline markets. BAAJA grid provisions could cost developers $35B; states could extract $136B more. Data center capacity is projected to grow 180 GW (+23% annually) through 2030 with energy as the primary bottleneck.

bullets.title: BTDR down ~15% on direct Malaysia data center exposure to new US export controls
bullets.body: Bit Digital (BTDR) fell 13–15% with options volume surging 273% to 77K contracts as its 153MW Malaysia pipeline faces direct risk from the BIS rule restricting chip access through SE Asian data centers. Malaysia has 61 data center projects totaling 8,350MW in development; US-based hyperscalers expected to have relatively uninterrupted access, but non-US-linked demand is at risk.

bullets.title: AMD closes $8.2B World Labs acquisition; TensorWave signs 457MW OpenAI deal with AMD GPUs
bullets.body: AMD completed its all-stock acquisition of World Labs (spatial intelligence/robotics AI) for ~$8.2B, with Fei-Fei Li joining as EVP and chief scientist. Separately, TensorWave signed a six-year, 457MW deal with OpenAI using AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs (Helios rack-scale), with infrastructure expected online H1 2027—a meaningful non-NVDA AI infrastructure win.

bullets.title: AI CX spend surging; Anthropic launches Microsoft-competitive productivity suite; OpenAI revenue ~$50B run rate
bullets.body: Ramp data shows AI customer experience spend jumped to 13.3% of classified spend from 0.8% in June. Anthropic launched Claude Whiteboards, Sheets, Dashboards, and Meetings as a direct competitive threat to Microsoft's franchise. Anthropic also cut Claude pricing 20% and improved output speed 30%. OpenAI annualized revenue run rate near $50B with enterprise revenue now ~50% of mix.

bullets.title: Cybersecurity spending to grow from ~1.5% to ~2.5% of enterprise AI budgets by 2028; ~23% CAGR
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley channel checks with AI risk and national security experts project cybersecurity spending rising from ~1.5% to ~2.5% of enterprise AI budgets by 2028, implying a ~23% cyber market CAGR. AI is lowering the expertise barrier for sophisticated attacks, and proliferation of local AI agents increases endpoint security importance—a structural tailwind for existing endpoint and network incumbents.

bullets.title: JPM Asia semi conference: bearish tone even among longs; RSI efficiency seen as demand headwind
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Day 1 Asia meetings showed a predominantly bearish tone in semis even among holders of NVDA and AVGO longs. Key concerns: NVDA leadership transition, insider selling risk, margin pressure from frontier LLM efficiency, and regulatory capture fears. Softbank's $3.73B charge to unwind Ohio turbine orders was cited as a major warning signal for power/ROI headwinds. TSM viewed as a 'funding long'; Korea memory seen as very cheap with 1Q HBM price hikes expected.

bullets.title: China economic data misses; BABA cloud revenue at risk from GPU ban; BABA at 52-week low
bullets.body: China retail sales, industrial production, and FAI all missed expectations, with property adjustment and deleveraging continuing to weigh. BABA is down 42.3% YTD at a 52-week low, and MS estimates ~8% of BABA's F28 and 17-20% of F29-31 cloud revenue is at risk from a potential GPU ban. The Trump-Xi meeting is set for November 19 in Shenzhen.

bullets.title: Container shipping beats: COSCO profits +80% YoY, Evergreen +114% YoY; spot rates +75-146% YoY
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised FY26/27 forecasts for COSCO by ~60%/45% and Evergreen by ~30%/30% after strong 3Q beats. Spot rates (SCFI, CCFI, Drewry's WCI) are up 75-146% YoY; Port of LA hit record throughput of 1.04M TEUs in September (+25% YoY). Panama Canal increased Neopanamax transits to 10 and raised max draft to 49 feet, reducing rerouting risk. Demand is shifting to cleantech, autos, and intra-regional trade.

bullets.title: CIO budgets improving +4% in 2026; software fastest-growing segment; 64% of CIOs prefer to procure AI
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley AlphaWise CIO survey shows IT budget growth accelerating (+4.0% 2026E, +23bps QoQ) with software the fastest-growing segment at +4.3%. 64% of CIOs prefer to procure AI rather than build it internally. Microsoft remains the leading GenAI beneficiary though LLM providers are gaining share. Data center costs are up 12% YoY and expected to rise 15% annually over the next two years.
